scope: Add targeted behavior coverage for three existing password controls without changing authentication policy or claiming full requirement verification.

V6.2.1.observation: The existing 12-character policy exceeds the ASVS v5.0.0 Level 1 mandatory minimum of 8; the standard strongly recommends 15. The test verifies 11/12 and 256/257 boundaries. Manual review must cover every account creation/replacement path and disposition the recommendation.

V6.2.5.observation: The shared password schema accepts lower/uppercase, numeric-only, punctuation-only, leading/trailing whitespace and Unicode examples without composition rules. This is representative behavioral evidence, not exhaustive input coverage or manual review.

V6.2.8.observation: A real sign-in API control accepts the exact Unicode password used to create the account hash and rejects uppercase, trailing-space and canonically decomposed variants. Exact verification on password change and remaining flows still needs review.

policy.current: 12-character minimum; maximum 256; scrypt hashes the submitted password.
policy.strongRecommendation: ASVS Level 1 strongly recommends a 15-character minimum; it is not silently adopted or waived.

finalSource.method: Sorted unique git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z -- packages tools plugin; hash path+NUL+bytes+NUL.

actualBundledJourneys.scope: Final shipped kernel drives complete starter scaffold and loan feature plus the brownfield CLI/library repair fixture. Exact app/browser case counts are asserted in the real generated project.

inventoryState.QLT02: Unmapped and unqualified; no structural, semantic or qualification status changed.

privacyScan.scope: All added tracked and untracked lines against HEAD, scanned without staging or changing the user's index.
privacyScan.disposition: Both findings are the literal [redacted] expected-output markers in the synthetic logging redaction test (logging.test.ts:30-31); they are not credentials. The scanner's assignment heuristic flags these deliberate redaction assertions.

limits: Representative tests do not establish full ASVS requirements, independent security review, password-change equivalence, usability/password-manager behavior, host or deployment assurance, or product policy approval.
